newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council expected to vote on Boutros Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: UN Council expected to vote on Boutros Tuesday.

text.p: The United Nations Security Council is expected to vote on the candidacy of Boutros Boutros-Ghali for a second five-year term on Tuesday, diplomats said late on Monday.

The vote on a resolution by three African states was to have been held on Monday but council members discussed procedures most of the day. U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright came to the meetings, with instructions to block a second term for Boutros-Ghali.

The voting will be by secret ballot. Egypt's Ambassador Nabil Elaraby said he expected that all delegataions except the United States would vote in favour of the resolution supporting Boutros-Ghali in the post "until the year 2001."

The purpose of the resolution is to put on record the council's overwhelming support for Boutros-Ghali and in the process isolate the United States, which has been strongly criticised for its position on Boutros-Ghali and for owing $1.4 billion in dues and peacekeeping contributions.

Albright's spokesman, James Rubin, said the ambassador had received written instructions from Washington to oppose Boutros-Ghali's candidacy. He said the U.S. Congress had lost confidence in Boutros-Ghali and his re-election "would make it virtually impossible for us to obtain the hundreds of millions of dollars that we need to pay back the United Nations."
